The identity behind a set of OIDC claims, **auto-creating the user on
first login** — the exact branch `/auth` runs once a token is validated,
minus the validation.

Named for the protocol, not the IdP: the claims read here (`sub`, `email`,
`given_name`, `family_name`, `picture`) are OIDC standard ones, so a caller
fronting a different provider needs no new route. Keycloak is what issues
them in this deployment, and `users.keycloak_id` is where `sub` lands —
hence the service layer below keeps its name.

The caller posts the decoded token (only `sub` is read to resolve; the rest
feeds the row when it has to be created). Unknown `sub` with no `email` is
a 401, same as `/auth`: a user row without an email is not created.

Takes the claims as a body rather than a path segment because that is what
creation needs, and POST because the call can write.

Same response as `/auth/by-api-key` — the identity `/auth` mints for an
OAuth2 session: no scope ceiling, no project confinement. `token` is null
here, unlike in `/auth`, because the route is addressed by claims and never
sees the bearer; the caller already holds it and fills it in if it needs to
pass the identity on.

get.description:
Resolve an `sk_` api-key to the identity it authenticates as (401 when

The returned identity carries the key's scope ceiling and project — both
still enforced downstream by `MembershipService`.

The key travels in the path, so it lands in the access logs of whatever
sits in front of this pod. Acceptable only because `/internal` never leaves
the cluster; anything routing it elsewhere needs the key moved to a body.

post.description:
Whether the caller may do something to one resource — the same verdict
every endpoint in this service enforces, exposed for services that hold an
identity but not the membership tree.

The identity comes from the relayed `x-user` header, and it has to: the
check intersects two axes, the user's **role** on the resource (inherited up
the `parent_id` chain) and the **ceiling** their credential carries. Only
the JWT has the second. Passing a bare user id instead would silently widen
an api-key beyond the scopes and the single project it was confined to,
which is the one mistake this route exists to prevent.

Name the scope explicitly (`datasets:read`) when the caller knows the type,
or send `action: read|write` to have it derived from the resource's own
type — the polymorphic form, for a caller holding only an id.

**A denial is a 200**, with `reason` saying which step failed: no such
resource, no membership, a role that does not reach, or a credential ceiling
or project confinement narrowing it. A 4xx here means the *check* failed,
which is a different thing a caller must handle differently.

The project an inference call is attributed to, and whether the plan of
its organization still allows LLM calls this month — for auth-service, which
puts both in the identity it signs for the inference gateway
(`app/services/llm_usage.py`).

The identity is the relayed `x-user`, as for `/permissions/check`: an
api-key confined to one project must not be attributed to another. The
project is the one asked for (`x-gwenlake-project`, read by auth-service)
or the credential's own; it is kept only if the caller may read it.

A call with no project counts for no organization, and is refused only
when every organization the caller works in is blocked (`llm_usage.access`).

get.description:

plan counts them, so a client shows that rather than recounting members. The

The LLM spend of the month so far against what the plan includes, in

false` means this deployment does not count (no inference database): the
quota is then contractual only and nothing is blocked.

get.description:
One file's bytes (`Connection(...).filesystem().open(path)`). Read-only:
a connection is a source, never a destination — a transform writes into
its output dataset.

Streamed from connection-service as it arrives, so the pod holds a chunk at
a time whatever the file's size. A source that fails part-way can only cut
the body short — the status is sent — and the client sees a truncated
transfer rather than a short file: a 200 is chunked, with no length, and a
206 declares its `Content-Length`.

**Part of the file** with a standard `Range` header holding one range of
bytes (`parse_range`): connection-service seeks where the connector can
(`download_range`: smb, s3, gcs, azureblob) and the answer is a 206 with
`Content-Range`, `Content-Length` and `Accept-Ranges` relayed — how a
reader that needs the head of a 6.5 GB clip and the index at its end moves
a few MB of it. A connector that cannot seek ignores the range and sends
the whole file as a 200 (`Accept-Ranges: none`); the caller tells by the
status. A range that starts at or past the end is a 416 whose
`Content-Range: bytes */size` gives the size. A header this relay does not
take — another unit, several ranges, a malformed one — is ignored, as RFC
9110 allows: the whole file, a 200. `bytes=-0` is a 416 with no size, no
source being asked.

get.description:
Télécharger un fichier du modèle, par son nom.

    GET /v1/mlmodels/{id}/resolve/main/model.safetensors

La forme est celle du Hub Hugging Face, délibérément : c'est ce qu'un
outil de chargement sait déjà consommer, et ce qu'un utilisateur sait déjà
lire.

`revision` est une référence git du dépôt du modèle — une branche, un tag,
un commit. C'est là que vit le pointeur, donc c'est lui qui décide QUELLE
version des poids est servie : demander un commit ancien rend les octets
de ce jour-là, sans qu'on ait eu à les dupliquer.

Le flux passe par ici plutôt que par une redirection vers le stockage :
celui-ci n'est pas joignable depuis l'extérieur, et c'est voulu. Le
contrôle d'accès reste donc là où il est vérifiable.

Ce que ce modèle contient, à cette révision.

À lire avant `resolve` : les noms viennent du code qui a entraîné, pas
d'une convention, et rien d'autre ne les publie.

post.description:
Parmi ces empreintes, lesquelles ne sont pas encore stockées ?

put.description:
Dépose les octets d'un artefact, adressés par leur empreinte.

    PUT /v1/mlmodels/{id}/artifacts/sha256:6459f36a...

L'empreinte est **recalculée** pendant l'écriture et comparée à celle de
l'URL. Un stockage adressé par contenu dont le contenu ne correspond pas à
son adresse ne se répare pas : la clé serait ensuite servie pour tout
fichier qui prétend cette empreinte, et le modèle chargerait des octets
étrangers sans que rien ne le signale.

Rien n'est publié ici. Le fichier n'appartient au modèle que lorsqu'un
commit porte le pointeur qui le nomme — jusque-là ce sont des octets
stockés que personne ne réclame.

post.description:
Fork `root_id`'s lineage cone (ancestors ∪ descendants) onto a new Iceberg branch.

Creates the Iceberg branch on every Iceberg dataset of the cone (copy-on-write
off `from_branch`), so the branch starts as a snapshot of trunk and can be
evolved in isolation. Non-Iceberg datasets are skipped. With `build=true`,
also rebuilds `root_id`'s upstream chain on the new branch. `datasets:write`
is pre-checked on every dataset before the first branch is created.

Promote (merge) an Iceberg branch into trunk across `root_id`'s lineage cone.

On every Iceberg dataset carrying branch `name`, fast-forwards 'main' to the
branch's current snapshot; datasets without the branch are left untouched.
With `delete_branch=true` the branch refs are dropped after promotion. The
pre-merge trunk snapshots stay until expiration, so the operation is
revertible via Iceberg snapshot history. 404 when no dataset carries the branch.

post.description:
Trigger an async scan of a repository's code for producer declarations.

The worker clones the repository (at `ref` when given, else the default
branch), extracts `@transform_df` (Python) and `-- @output/@input` (SQL)
declarations, resolves their paths to dataset ids, and upserts the
corresponding `python`/`sql` transform resources. Non-default refs are
additive: they only create/update/delete transforms born on that branch.
Returns 202 immediately; poll the resulting builds or logs for the outcome.

get.description:
Poll an async orchestration task (repository scan / lineage propagate) by id.

Reads the task state from the celery result backend. `ready` is True once the
worker finished; on success `result` holds the task's return payload (e.g. a
scan's edges_created / warnings), on failure `error` holds the message. Task
ids are opaque and unguessable, so any authenticated caller may poll one.

Ce que le run a écrit, pendant qu'il tourne.

`error_message` ne porte la sortie qu'une fois le build terminé, et
seulement sa fin : tant qu'un entraînement tourne, il n'y a rien à lire.
Suivre une préparation de données ou une courbe de perte demandait donc un
accès au cluster, que personne n'a depuis une interface ou un agent.

Un entraînement délégué au pool a ses journaux chez train-service. Un
transform local (python, function) écrit sa sortie ligne à ligne dans
Redis pendant qu'il tourne (`app/services/build_logs.py`) : `source` vaut
alors `live`. Une fois le build fini et la liste Redis expirée, le journal
complet est relu sur le stockage de l'organisation (`stored`). Les builds
SQL et les syncs n'ont pas de sortie de processus : `logs` est `null`.

Lire le journal demande `builds:read`, comme le build : il contient ce que
le transform a imprimé, secrets compris s'il en a imprimé.

Klara's identity and instructions — the definition shipped with this
deployment, identical for every organization.

post.description:
Start a conversation and run its first turn.

The reply carries `session_id`; continue the thread by posting to
`/klara/{session_id}`. A failed first turn leaves no empty session behind —
the row is created only once the turn succeeds, so a broken credential or an
unreachable model does not litter the history.

get.description:
The tools Klara can use. `writes` marks the ones that change something.

Without `project_id` this is the shipped set — the workspace capabilities,
identical for everyone. With one, it also lists the project's datasets,
ontologies and mediasets: in a project those are connected automatically,
so this is what a turn there would actually see.

parameters.name: project_id

schema.description: Include the resources of this project, as a run in it would.
schema.title: Project Id

parameters.description: Include the resources of this project, as a run in it would.

post.description:
Run one of Klara's tools — a workspace capability, or a capability of a
resource in the current project.

This is the loopback a run takes: the in-process runner posts here with the
caller's identity re-encoded, so a tool call from the model and a tool call
from a client follow exactly the same path and the same checks. There is no
gate here beyond the identity — each capability performs its own, because
only it knows which resource and which scope its arguments imply. For a
resource tool that means the resource's own read scope, checked against the
**caller**: Klara reaches exactly what the person talking to it reaches.

The name is resolved by rebuilding the manifest and matching the entry, the
way `/agents/{id}/tools/{name}/invoke` does — never by parsing the name,
whose two halves are sanitized and may be deduplicated.

parameters.name: project_id

schema.description: The project whose resources the tool belongs to, for a resource tool.
schema.title: Project Id

parameters.description: The project whose resources the tool belongs to, for a resource tool.

post.description:
Continue a conversation. The history is replayed to the model server-side.

The context is resolved again per turn: a UI that navigates from one project
to another mid-conversation should have Klara follow, and re-resolving is
what makes the *current* project current rather than the one the thread
started in.

get.description:
Your own conversations. Private to their creator — Klara is reachable by
everyone, which makes the creator check the only thing separating two
users' histories.

One dataset as an OpenLineage `DatasetEvent`.

A `res.model.*` is answered here too: to OpenLineage a model *is* a dataset
— data a job produces and another consumes — and the spec has no third
entity for it.

One `transform` or `sync` as a `JobEvent` — its declared inputs and
outputs, with no run attached.

One build as a `RunEvent`.

The `eventType` reflects the build's current status, so a running build is
`RUNNING` and a finished one `COMPLETE`/`FAIL`/`ABORT` — this renders the
state now, where the emitted events recorded the transitions.

A whole project as design-time events — every dataset, then every job.

Datasets first so a consumer processing the list in order never meets a
reference before its declaration.

post.description:
Run a read-only statement. Without a LIMIT of its own, the result is
capped (1000 rows unless `limit` says otherwise); a cut is reported — in
the JSON body (`truncated`, `limit`) and, for every format, in the
`X-Gwenlake-Truncated` / `X-Gwenlake-Row-Limit` headers — so a client
reading a whole table can tell it must page.

Accessible sql-queries (summaries — the SQL text comes with the
single-query GET, which reads it from the storage backend).

A `sql` change on a non-main branch stores a branch copy: builds on

The SQL text as it was at `version_id` (restore it by PATCHing it back).

ActionRule.title: ActionRule
ActionRule.description:
A precondition on an object the action was given.

Read as: *this property of that parameter must satisfy this comparison, or
the action does not apply.* Which is what makes an action a transition
rather than a blind write — "approve a claim" is only valid on a claim that
was submitted.

`message` is what a user should be told when it fails; without one the
message has to be reconstructed from the fields, and it always reads worse
than a sentence written by whoever knew why the rule exists.

ActionType-Input.title: ActionType
ActionType-Input.description:
The third pillar: what may be *done* to the objects and links.

An action is parameterized, guarded by `rules`, permitted by a `scope`, and
performs one or more `operations`. Together those say "who may do this, to
what, when, and with what effect" — which is the whole of what a caller
needs to know before invoking one, and the whole of what an executor needs
to enforce.

**Still declarative: nothing here is executed server-side.** It is a
published contract, and the validation below is what keeps it honest — an
action that names a property no object type has, or a rule on a parameter
that does not exist, is refused at save time rather than discovered by
whoever eventually wires the executor.

ActionType-Output.title: ActionType
ActionType-Output.description:
The third pillar: what may be *done* to the objects and links.

An action is parameterized, guarded by `rules`, permitted by a `scope`, and
performs one or more `operations`. Together those say "who may do this, to
what, when, and with what effect" — which is the whole of what a caller
needs to know before invoking one, and the whole of what an executor needs
to enforce.

**Still declarative: nothing here is executed server-side.** It is a
published contract, and the validation below is what keeps it honest — an
action that names a property no object type has, or a rule on a parameter
that does not exist, is refused at save time rather than discovered by
whoever eventually wires the executor.

AgentMCPServer.title: AgentMCPServer
AgentMCPServer.description:
One `mcp` entry of an agent definition: either a **`tool` resource** of
the project (`id` = `res.tool.*`, or `ref` = `<project>.<alias>` / a bare
alias — its MCP server and encrypted headers live on the tool), or an
inline **remote** MCP server (`url`, ...). Either way the server's tools
are fetched and advertised to the LLM at run time. SSE only — a stdio
server would run an arbitrary command inside the catalog.

AgentResourceBinding.title: AgentResourceBinding
AgentResourceBinding.description:
One `resources` entry of an agent definition: a bindable resource
(`id`) or an alias reference (`ref`, `<project>.<alias>` or a bare alias
in the agent's own project), optionally restricted to a subset of the
type's capabilities (`tools`; omitted = all).

AgentSessionRequest.title: AgentSessionRequest
AgentSessionRequest.description:
Body of `POST /agents/{id}/sessions` (new session + first turn) and
`POST /agents/{id}/sessions/{session_id}` (next turn). The conversation
history lives on the session server-side — only the new `input` travels.
Definition fields come from the stored, versioned agent; `model` is an
optional per-turn override.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Scope ceiling for the key. Omit for a key that inherits every scope its owner's role grants; pass a list to narrow it (e.g. ['datasets:read', 'sql:read'] for a read-only key). A key can never exceed its owner's role.

ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated
ApiKeyCreated.description: Returned only on creation — plain key is never stored and never shown again.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: Correlates all builds of this trigger.

builds.title: Builds
builds.description: Builds in topological order; the last one is the target.

BuildBatchResponse.title: BuildBatchResponse
BuildBatchResponse.description:
Result of triggering a build: one `Build` row per node of the resolved
DAG, chained in topological order on the celery queue.

target_only.title: Target Only
target_only.description: Build the target alone, ignoring upstream.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: Iceberg data branch to build into (default 'main').

outputs.title: Outputs
outputs.description: Every dataset this build rewrites: the target first, then the other outputs of a decorated function declaring several (one build runs the function once and refreshes them all).

ConnectionCreate.title: ConnectionCreate
ConnectionCreate.description:
Create payload: the identity this service owns, plus the configuration it
forwards. `configuration.type` selects the datasource type and cannot be
changed afterwards.

ConnectionCredentialsUpdate.title: ConnectionCredentialsUpdate
ConnectionCredentialsUpdate.description:
`PUT /connections/{id}/credentials` — rotate the secrets.

Replaced wholesale rather than merged: a half-applied rotation leaves a
connection authenticating with neither the old secret nor the new one.

type.title: Type
type.description: The datasource type. Immutable — set at creation, never patched.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: The stored configuration, credentials absent by construction. Present on `GET /connections/{id}`; omitted from list responses, which would need one call to connection-service per row.

credential_fields.title: Credential Fields
credential_fields.description: The names of the fields that are secret for this type — what a form renders as masked inputs with 'leave blank to keep'.

ConnectionQueryRequest.title: ConnectionQueryRequest
ConnectionQueryRequest.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/query` — run a query in the connection's native
language (SQL for postgresql/mysql, SOQL for salesforce) against its
datasource. This is the only query surface for connections;
`/sql/statements` is dataset-only.

ConnectionTestRequest.title: ConnectionTestRequest
ConnectionTestRequest.description:
`POST /connections/test` — test a configuration nobody has saved.

The create form's button, and the only route here that takes a configuration
instead of an id: a password typed but not yet saved is precisely not the
configuration an id designates.

`project_id` is the project the connection is being created in. The test
is authorized as the create would be (`connections:write` there): it makes
connection-service open a socket to the typed host from inside the cluster,
which is not something any identity — a narrow api-key included — may do.

ConnectionUpdate.title: ConnectionUpdate
ConnectionUpdate.description:
Patch payload. Every field is optional; omit one to leave it unchanged.

A `configuration` PATCH is **merged**, not replaced, so changing a host does
not mean resending a password. `type` cannot be changed — a connection that
became a different datasource is a different connection, and the id is what
17 syncs point at.

CreateObjectOperation.title: CreateObjectOperation
CreateObjectOperation.description:
Bring a new object into being, with its properties set.

Names the object *type* rather than a parameter, because there is nothing
to point at yet — which is the difference from every other operation.
`assign_to_parameter` binds the result to a parameter name so a later
operation in the same action can link to it.

DatasetPatch.title: DatasetPatch
DatasetPatch.description:
PATCH body — all fields optional so the alias can be changed alone.
`type` is not defaulted here: an omitted `type` leaves it untouched.

DatasetSearchRequest.title: DatasetSearchRequest
DatasetSearchRequest.description:
Body of `POST /datasets/{id}/search` — semantic search over a vector
dataset. Either `query` (embedded with the dataset's model, as the caller)
or a ready-made `vector`; `where` is an optional SQL filter on the
metadata columns (`path = 'a.pdf'`).

DatasetSummary.title: DatasetSummary
DatasetSummary.description:
Unified storage summary for a dataset, regardless of `type`.

- iceberg: read from the table's current snapshot summary (exact, cheap).
  `num_files` is always None — the table's internal data-file count is an
  implementation detail, not a user-visible file count.
- files: aggregated from the dataset's stored files; `num_rows` is counted
  over the Parquet files (None when none are present / countable).
- vector: `num_rows` is the LanceDB table's row count, `dimensions` the
  vector width and `model` the embedding model; `num_files`/`size_bytes`
  walk the table's storage.

Fields are `None` when unknown (e.g. an Iceberg table with no data yet, or a
file dataset with no Parquet).

DeleteObjectOperation.title: DeleteObjectOperation
DeleteObjectOperation.description:
Remove an object. Its links go with it — an object that is gone cannot
be an endpoint, and leaving dangling ones would make the graph lie.

FolderPatch.title: FolderPatch
FolderPatch.description: PATCH body — all fields optional so the alias can be changed alone.

GitChange.title: GitChange
GitChange.description:
A single file change to apply in a commit.

`upsert` creates or overwrites the file at `path` with `content` (decoded
per `encoding`). `delete` removes the file; `content` is ignored.

GitCommitRequest.title: GitCommitRequest
GitCommitRequest.description: Commit a set of file changes onto `ref` and push to the remote.

GitImportRequest.title: GitImportRequest
GitImportRequest.description:
Import a single file from a repository into an existing dataset.
`dataset_id` is required and must belong to a project the caller has access to.

IcebergColumn.title: IcebergColumn
IcebergColumn.description:
One column of an explicitly declared Iceberg schema. `type` is a type name
(string/long/double/timestamp/...) resolved by `app.services.iceberg`.
`required` columns are non-nullable; key columns are forced required.

IcebergConfig.title: IcebergConfig
IcebergConfig.description:
Iceberg catalog config for an organization. The catalog is JDBC-backed
(PostgreSQL). `warehouse` defaults server-side to `s3://{org_bucket}/iceberg`
when omitted. `credentials` holds the catalog DB user/password — write-only.

IcebergKeys.title: IcebergKeys
IcebergKeys.description:
Body for `PUT /datasets/{id}/keys` — the identifier (key) columns
used by the UPDATE (upsert) write mode.

organization_id.title: Organization Id
organization_id.description: The organization this conversation is about (res.organization.*).

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: The project the caller is currently in (res.project.*). Implies its organization, so passing both is redundant but harmless.

KlaraSessionRequest.title: KlaraSessionRequest
KlaraSessionRequest.description:
One turn of a conversation with Klara.

Both context fields are optional and are resolved in this order: the project
when given (its organization comes with it), then the organization, then —
only if the caller can see exactly one — inference. With several and no
hint, Klara is told to ask rather than pick.

They are re-read on **every** turn, not just the first: a UI that navigates
to another project mid-conversation should have Klara follow.

build.title: Build
build.description: Also build root's upstream chain on the new branch.

LineageBranchCreate.title: LineageBranchCreate
LineageBranchCreate.description: Fork the whole connected lineage of `root_id` onto a new Iceberg branch.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: Iceberg datasets the branch was dropped from.

skipped.title: Skipped
skipped.description: Cone nodes without the branch (or non-Iceberg), left untouched.

LineageBranchDeleteResponse.title: LineageBranchDeleteResponse
LineageBranchDeleteResponse.description: Result of a lineage-wide branch deletion.

delete_branch.title: Delete Branch
delete_branch.description: Also drop the branch after promoting it.

LineageBranchMerge.title: LineageBranchMerge
LineageBranchMerge.description: Promote (merge) an Iceberg branch into trunk across a lineage cone.

merged.title: Merged
merged.description: Iceberg datasets whose trunk was fast-forwarded to the branch.

skipped.title: Skipped
skipped.description: Cone nodes without the branch (or non-Iceberg), left untouched.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: Whether the branch refs were dropped after the merge.

LineageBranchMergeResponse.title: LineageBranchMergeResponse
LineageBranchMergeResponse.description: Result of a lineage-branch merge (fast-forward of trunk on each dataset).

branched.title: Branched
branched.description: Iceberg datasets a branch was created on.

LineageGraph.title: LineageGraph
LineageGraph.description: A sub-graph rooted at `root_id`, for UI rendering.

LineagePropagateResponse.title: LineagePropagateResponse
LineagePropagateResponse.description:
Acknowledgment of a downstream-propagation trigger. The descendant builds
are resolved and created asynchronously by the worker task `task_id`; poll
them via GET /orchestration/builds?target_id=... once it runs.

LinkOperation.title: LinkOperation
LinkOperation.description:
Create or remove one typed link between two objects the action holds.

Both endpoints are parameters, never types: a link joins two *instances*,
and naming a type here would leave the operation unable to say which one.

LinkType.title: LinkType
LinkType.description:
A typed link between object types.

`source_object_type` / `target_object_type` accept a single name, a list of
alternatives, or None (untyped). Endpoints may reference object_type
api_names **or** their subtypes. Only single-name links can be traversed
by the `/objects/.../links/...` endpoints.

Binding, one of:
- `foreign_key_property`: a property on the **target** object type holding
  the source object's primary key (ONE_TO_ONE / ONE_TO_MANY);
- `dataset_id` + `source_key`/`target_key`: an edge dataset whose columns
  hold the primary keys of both sides (any cardinality).

LlmAccessDecision.title: LlmAccessDecision
LlmAccessDecision.description:
What auth-service puts in the identity it signs for the inference
gateway. `project_id` is the project the call is attributed to — null when
none was asked for, or when the caller may not use the one asked for (it
is then not sent: a project the caller cannot read must not be charged).
`llm_blocked` is the plan's verdict for that project's organization.

LlmAccessRequest.title: LlmAccessRequest
LlmAccessRequest.description:
The project an inference call is made for — the `x-gwenlake-project`
the caller sent, as auth-service read it. Absent: the credential's own
project (an api-key's), else none.

MCPCredentials.title: MCPCredentials
MCPCredentials.description:
The secret half of an MCP tool, write-only — encrypted at rest, never
returned. Static `headers` sent to the server (an `Authorization` value,
an API key), or an OAuth2 client (`client_id` + `client_secret`) exchanged
for an access token when `auth` is `client_credentials`. An empty object
clears what is stored.

MCPToolConfig.title: MCPToolConfig
MCPToolConfig.description:
A remote MCP server, SSE transport only (a stdio server would run a
command inside the catalog). `auth` says how it is authenticated to:
`headers` (the default) or `client_credentials` (OAuth2 — needs
`token_url`, optionally `scope`).

MCPToolConfigInfo.title: MCPToolConfigInfo
MCPToolConfigInfo.description:
Response shape — no credentials field at all; `has_credentials` says
whether something is stored.

MediasetPatch.title: MediasetPatch
MediasetPatch.description:
PATCH body — all fields optional. `media_type` is immutable (a matching
value is accepted, a different one is a 400).

MediasetSummary.title: MediasetSummary
MediasetSummary.description:
Storage summary of a mediaset, aggregated from its stored files.
`files_by_format` counts the files admitted per format of the media type.

version.title: Version
version.description: Free-form label; the reproducible version is `git_sha`.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Model parameters (hyperparameters, thresholds), handed to runs as CATALOG_MODEL_PARAMETERS.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: Evaluation metrics of the last training run.

repository_id.title: Repository Id
repository_id.description: The git repository holding the model's files.

path.title: Path
path.description: Directory of the model inside the repository. Handed to runs as CATALOG_MODEL_PATH; a training run commits what it writes there.

ModelCreate.title: ModelCreate
ModelCreate.description:
Create a model in a project. Its artifacts live in the referenced
repository under `path` — nothing is stored on the platform's file store.

ModelInfo.title: ModelInfo
ModelInfo.description:
Response shape. Credentials never appear — they live on the referenced
repository and are decrypted at run time.

ModelUpdate.title: ModelUpdate
ModelUpdate.description:
PATCH payload — every field optional; the service re-validates the merged
state. `parameters`/`metrics` replace wholesale.

ModifyObjectOperation.title: ModifyObjectOperation
ModifyObjectOperation.description: Write properties onto an object the action was given as a parameter.

NodePosition.title: NodePosition
NodePosition.description:
Where a node sits in the project's workflow drawing, in the editor's
canvas coordinates.

OidcClaims.title: OidcClaims
OidcClaims.description:
The claims `UserService.create_from_keycloak` reads out of a decoded
OIDC token — Keycloak's in this deployment, but every field here is a
standard claim (`sub` from JWT itself, the rest from OIDC's `profile` and
`email` scopes), so nothing in this shape is IdP-specific.

Extra claims are accepted and ignored, so a caller can post the decoded
token verbatim instead of picking it apart. Only `sub` is required — it is
what resolves an existing user; the rest is needed solely when the row has
to be created, and a missing `email` is a 401 at that point (`/auth` does
not auto-create a user without one either), not a 422 upfront.

OntologyCreate.title: OntologyCreate
OntologyCreate.description:
Create payload — the ontology spec, flat (no `ontology` wrapper).
`api_name` is the ontology's stable identifier; `name` defaults to it.

OntologyUpdate.title: OntologyUpdate
OntologyUpdate.description:
Patch payload. `object_types` / `link_types` / `action_types`, when
present, replace the stored lists wholesale — send the full updated list.
Cross-references are re-validated by the service against the merged state.

OrganizationMemberPostSchema.title: OrganizationMemberPostSchema
OrganizationMemberPostSchema.description:
Identify the member by `id` or by `email` (at least one is required).
When both are given, `id` takes precedence.

ParameterValueModification.title: ParameterValueModification
ParameterValueModification.description: Copies the value of an action parameter into the property.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: An explicit scope, e.g. `datasets:read`. Mutually exclusive with `action`.

action.title: Action
action.description: `read` or `write`, resolved against the resource's own type. Mutually exclusive with `scope`.

resource_type.title: Resource Type
resource_type.description: Assert the resource is of this type; a mismatch is `allowed: false`.

PermissionCheck.title: PermissionCheck
PermissionCheck.description:
Ask whether the caller may do something to one resource.

Exactly one of `scope` and `action`, and the difference is who knows the
resource's type. `scope` is the explicit form — `datasets:read` — for a
caller that already knows what it is addressing. `action` (`read`/`write`)
is the polymorphic one: the scope is derived from the resource's own type,
which is what a caller holding only an id wants, and mirrors what
`MembershipService.require_resource` does for `/filesystem` and
`/orchestration`.

`resource_type`, when given, additionally asserts the resource *is* of that
type, so a dataset id passed where a connection was expected answers "no"
rather than being checked against the wrong resource.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: The scope actually checked — resolved from `action` when that was sent.

role.title: Role
role.description: The caller's strongest role on the resource, inherited grants included.

ceiling_applied.title: Ceiling Applied
ceiling_applied.description: True when the credential carries a scope ceiling (an api-key), which can only narrow the role.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it was denied. Null when allowed.

PermissionDecision.title: PermissionDecision
PermissionDecision.description:
The answer, and enough of the reasoning to act on it.

A denial is a 200 with `allowed: false`, not a 403: this route *reports* a
verdict rather than enforcing one, and a caller that has to read an HTTP
error as data cannot tell "denied" from "the check itself failed".

`role` and `scope` are what make a denial actionable — whether the user has
no membership at all, or a role that does not reach far enough, or a
credential ceiling narrowing it (`ceiling_applied`).

PropertyDef.title: PropertyDef
PropertyDef.description: One entry of an object_type's `properties` map.

RepositoryCreate.title: RepositoryCreate
RepositoryCreate.description:
Create payload. `configuration` is optional throughout.

With no URL the repository targets the configured git server and its clone
URL is derived from the resource alias. Credentials are optional too: a
public repository needs none, and an internal one falls back to the shared
service token.

RepositoryCredentialsUpdate.title: RepositoryCredentialsUpdate
RepositoryCredentialsUpdate.description:
`PUT /repositories/{id}/credentials` — rotate the token.

Replaced wholesale rather than merged: a half-applied rotation leaves a
repository authenticating with neither the old secret nor the new.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: `type` (always `git`), `url`, `provider`, `default_branch` — the token never appears. On a listing only the derived `url` is present: the rest would be one call to connection-service per row.

credential_fields.title: Credential Fields
credential_fields.description: Names of the fields that are secret — what a form masks.

RepositoryUpdate.title: RepositoryUpdate
RepositoryUpdate.description:
Patch payload. Every field is optional; omit one to leave it unchanged.

A `configuration` PATCH is **merged**, not replaced, so changing a provider
does not mean resending the token.

ResourceMove.title: ResourceMove
ResourceMove.description:
Body for `POST /filesystem/resources/{id}/move`. The new `project_id`
is derived from the parent (the parent itself if it's a project, or
`parent.project_id` if it's a folder).

ResourcePatch.title: ResourcePatch
ResourcePatch.description:
PATCH payload — like `ResourceBase` but every field is optional, so the
slug can be changed on its own (`ResourceBase` requires `name`, which makes
a slug-only update impossible). When a `name` is sent without a `slug`, the
slug is still regenerated from it (same rule as create/rename); sending only
`slug` (or the legacy `alias`) updates the slug and leaves the name untouched.

ResourceRename.title: ResourceRename
ResourceRename.description:
Body for `POST /filesystem/resources/{id}/rename`. When `slug` (or the
legacy `alias`) is omitted, it is regenerated from `name` (same as create).

SkillCreate.title: SkillCreate
SkillCreate.description:
A skill for agents — a `SKILL.md` (Agent Skills convention). Either
structured fields (`instructions` = the Markdown body, the frontmatter
fields beside it) or a raw `definition` (the whole file), never both.

sql.title: Sql
sql.description: The SQL text (versioned on the organization's storage backend).

SqlQueryCreate.title: SqlQueryCreate
SqlQueryCreate.description:
Create a sql-query in a project. `sql` is the query text — stored (and
versioned) on the organization's storage backend, never in the database.

SqlQueryInfo.title: SqlQueryInfo
SqlQueryInfo.description:
Response shape. `sql` is read back from the organization's storage
backend (single-query GET only; list responses omit it). `storage`
carries the current upload (`{path, version}`).

SqlQueryUpdate.title: SqlQueryUpdate
SqlQueryUpdate.description:
PATCH payload — every field optional. A `sql` change stores a new
version on the org's storage backend and re-derives the inputs of every
sql transform referencing this sql-query.

SqlQueryVersionContent.title: SqlQueryVersionContent
SqlQueryVersionContent.description: The SQL text at one version.

StatementsRequest.title: StatementsRequest
StatementsRequest.description:
`POST /sql/statements` — run a SQL statement live (ad hoc, nothing
stored). The *stored* form is the `sql-query` resource (`/sql/queries`,
`app/schemas/sql_queries.py`).

output.title: Output
output.description: The dataset or mediaset this sync writes into.

config.title: Config
config.description: Ingestion config: {'connection_id', 'mode'} plus source keys ('query'|'table' for table syncs, 'path_glob' for file syncs).

status.title: Status
status.description: celery task state: PENDING | STARTED | SUCCESS | FAILURE | ...

ready.title: Ready
ready.description: True once the task has finished (success or failure).

error.title: Error
error.description: Error message when the task failed.

TaskStatusResponse.title: TaskStatusResponse
TaskStatusResponse.description:
Status of an async orchestration task (repository scan / lineage propagate).

Polled via GET /orchestration/tasks/{task_id}. `ready` flips to True once the
worker has finished; `result` carries the task's return value on success (e.g.
a scan's `edges_created` / `warnings`), `error` the message on failure.

TimeTrigger.title: TimeTrigger
TimeTrigger.description: Cron-based trigger evaluated in a given IANA time zone.

output.title: Output
output.description: What this transform produces: a dataset (sql/python/function) or a model (train).

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: Upstream resource ids (datasets, plus models for python/train, a mediaset or connections for python; may be empty). For sql transforms, overridden by the sql-query's own `FROM/JOIN <project>.<dataset>` references.

config.title: Config
config.description: Producer config. sql: {'query_id'} (the sql-query holding the text). python / train: {'repository_id', 'entrypoint', 'packages'?, ...} (train also accepts 'commit_artifacts': false to skip the artifact commit). function: {'function', 'parameters'?} — the ready-made transform to run and its settings (GET /transforms/functions).

TransformCreate.title: TransformCreate
TransformCreate.description:
Create a transform in a project. The transform owns the producer wiring
(`inputs`/`output`); the lineage graph is derived from it.

input_count.title: Input Count
input_count.description: How many inputs the transform must declare.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: `config.parameters`, one descriptor per key, in form order.

TransformFunctionInfo.title: TransformFunctionInfo
TransformFunctionInfo.description:
One entry of the ready-made transform catalogue (`GET /transforms/functions`).

What a client needs to build the `config` of a `type: "function"` transform
and to wire it to the right resources: the name, what it reads, what kind of
dataset its output must be, and the `parameters` keys it understands.

TransformFunctionList.title: TransformFunctionList
TransformFunctionList.description:
The catalogue listing. A declared response model because this one *is*
the contract a client builds its form from — an untyped dict would publish
it in the docs as `{}`, which is the copy-in-the-client problem again.

TransformInfo.title: TransformInfo
TransformInfo.description:
Response shape. Credentials never appear (they live on the referenced
repository); the SQL text never appears either (it lives on the referenced
sql-query).

default.title: Default
default.description: What the function does when the key is absent. Show it as the placeholder and send nothing — the function owns its defaults, and writing them into a stored config freezes them.

TransformParameterInfo.title: TransformParameterInfo
TransformParameterInfo.description:
One `config.parameters` key of a transform function, described well
enough for a client to render a form field for it — which is the point of
publishing the catalogue rather than letting every client keep a copy.

TransformUpdate.title: TransformUpdate
TransformUpdate.description:
PATCH payload — every field optional; the service re-validates the merged
state (`type` + `output` + `inputs` + `config`) after applying it.

WorkflowPositions.title: WorkflowPositions
WorkflowPositions.description:
The project's layout: every placed resource and where. A resource
absent here has no position and takes the automatic layout.

WorkflowPositionsUpdate.title: WorkflowPositionsUpdate
WorkflowPositionsUpdate.description:
`PUT /orchestration/projects/{id}/positions`: the resources whose
position changes — `{x, y}` to place one, `null` to let the editor lay it
out again. Resources not named keep their position.
